clauses.text: THE TAXO TREE. Cargo → Equipable (utilities, provisions, weapon, wearables by SLOT — boots, coats, packs, charms) · Buildables (station, works) · Resources (wood — every cut and grade files under the one parent — metal, ceramic, lumen) · Consumables (food, medical, books) · Freight (post, trade) · Curios (relics, junk, contraband).
S.ledger holds marks per node or per item across five verbs — Deliver / Store / Donate / Scrap / Pickup — resolved item → leaf → root → default.

figure.note: the verbs read deliver, store, donate, scrap, pickup, and the defaults table holds those five

clauses.text: THE PARENT LAW is the sandbox standard done visibly: marking a parent clears every descendant override so the whole column under it flips as one, and a mixed column renders the half-bar tri-state.
THE DELIVERY DOSSIER (the pass and its toggles, with the donate-EXEMPT search box)
HAULIN' MANIFEST (the streamlined book — ONE take-mark over the category tree)
THE CARGO CHECKLIST (the in-depth book — a searchable grid where every category and item unfolds to its five marks; Enter opens the chain and lights the row)

figure.note: the found row stands with exactly five mark boxes, the grid's heads five words

clauses.text: full-word column heads on a 49px pitch

figure.note: every gap between the five heads, and between the boxes under them, measures 49 px

clauses.text: THE DOSSIER RUNS IN STRICT ORDER at any lit town: missions FIRST — the priority chain is accepted before anything else moves
Donate (exemptions held back)
Pickup (letters first, capacity honest)
One slip totals the pass.
The map rail carries the travel-options widget as sketched: run-on-arrival, grab all letters, deliver applicable
the on-arrival edge fires once per town with a cooldown, so riding past a door is never a surprise transaction
